title: Cohomology of a Zariski module agrees with that of its underlying abelian sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X_{\rm Zar}$ its small Zariski site [def-sc-zariski-site], and $\mathcal M$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $\mathcal M_{ab}$ for the underlying sheaf of abelian groups on $X_{\rm Zar}$. For every $q\geq0$ there is a canonical isomorphism $H^q(X,\mathcal M)\cong H^q(X_{\rm Zar},\mathcal M_{ab})$, where the left side is the right derived functor of global sections in $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-cohomology] and the right side is the right derived functor of global sections in abelian sheaves [def-sc-zariski-cohomology]. In degree zero this is the identity of $\Gamma(X,\mathcal M)$, and the isomorphisms are natural in every morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree), line 1862 and proof: the comparison for any ringed site and every object, specialized to the small Zariski site of a scheme; naturality follows from the uniqueness of universal delta-functors in the proof

proof.text: The reviewed comparison node [lem-sc-module-abelian-zariski-cohomology] states that for a scheme with its small Zariski site and any sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, the module-derived and underlying-abelian derived global sections are canonically isomorphic in every degree and naturally in the module sheaf. Applied to the present $X$ and $\mathcal M$, it gives the canonical isomorphisms $H^q(X,\mathcal M)\cong H^q(X_{\rm Zar},\mathcal M_{ab})$, natural in $\mathcal M$, which we take as the isomorphisms of the statement for $q\geq1$.

For $q=0$, both zeroth right-derived functors of a left exact functor are that functor: the module side is $H^0(X,\mathcal M)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal M)$ by [pqf-def-cohomology], and the abelian-sheaf side is $H^0(X_{\rm Zar},\mathcal M_{ab})=\mathcal M_{ab}(X)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal M)$ by [def-sc-zariski-cohomology] and the definition of the underlying sheaf. In degree zero we take as the isomorphism of the statement the identity of $\Gamma(X,\mathcal M)$ under these two identifications (the statement of [lem-sc-module-abelian-zariski-cohomology] does not say what its comparison is in degree zero, so it is not used there). The identity is canonical and natural in $\mathcal M$, since a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules acts on both sides by the same map on global sections. Together with step 1 this gives the canonical natural isomorphisms in every degree, the identity in degree zero.
